title: Quantile-driven adaptive thresholds for FlashAttention v2/v3 kernel fallback
creator: Elena Martinez
description: Introducing per-model, sequence-length aware adaptive thresholds to decide when to route attention ops to FlashAttention v2 vs v3 (and safe fallback) using empirically measured latency quantiles. This ticket implements the calibration job, runtime threshold evaluator (EWMA + hysteresis), and offline simulation harness to prevent oscillation and regressions seen in recent v3 rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration job collects 50k samples per model across common sequence-length buckets (8, 32, 128, 512) within 48h of run
Runtime uses model+len bucket thresholds computed from 95th/99th latency quantiles and applies EWMA smoothing with configurable alpha
No >5% increase in 99th percentile tail latency across canary traffic vs baseline during a 72h canary at 5% traffic
Automated simulation reproduces historical regression incident (incident-2026-01-prefill-jitter) and shows mitigation with new thresholds
Telemetry dashboards show per-route kernel-choice breakdown, GPU occupancy, and decode throughput; alerts created for abnormal kernel oscillation rates
technical_notes: We will bucket by model checkpoint, quantization profile, hardware class (A100-80GB / H100-80GB), and request max_seq_len to capture workload heterogeneity
Calibration collector runs as a low-priority job on dedicated profiling nodes; samples capture prefill vs decode latencies separately and record KV cache hit flag
Threshold computation uses 95th and 99th quantiles with a configurable safety margin (default +8%) to tolerate GC/warmup noise
Runtime evaluator applies EWMA(alpha=0.2) on observed quantiles and enforces hysteresis windows (min 30s) to avoid ping-ponging between kernels
If the runtime detects repeated oscillation, it falls back to a conservative static policy per-model for 10 minutes and emits an operational alert
We must ensure compatibility with existing kernel selector interface (KernelChoice v3) and not alter public API contracts
benchmarks: Offline sim: used historical trace from 2026-01 (2M requests) — adaptive thresholds reduced 99th tail latency by 12% compared to static v3-first rollout
Microbenchmarks: v3 wins for short seq (<=32) on H100; v2 remains better for long seq (>=512) on A100 until quantized kernels warm up
Cost model: adaptive routing lowers average GPU token-seconds by ~3% in simulated traffic due to better kernel-cost alignment
Canary staging (synthetic): at 5% traffic over 24h we saw two transient kernel switches but EWMA+hysteresis reduced switch rate by 78% vs naive thresholding
risks: Mis-calibrated thresholds could increase tail latency for critical routes; mitigation: rollouts start at 1% and have auto-rollback on threshold breaches
Profiling job sampling bias (cold-start heavy clients or synthetic tests) — we will stratify sampling and cross-validate with production shadow sampling
Increased complexity in telemetry and alerting — requires console dashboard work (separate ticket) and on-call runbook updates
Edge cases where model quantization changes behavior after fine-tuning — thresholds must be re-computed after model version changes
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Merge PRs and enable calibration job in staging (profiling nodes) — 2026-03-15
Phase 1: Run calibration for 48h, produce initial thresholds, run offline sim against 2M request trace — 2026-03-17
Phase 2: Canary rollout to 1% of traffic (us-west cluster) for 24h with strict alerting on 99th latency delta, kernel oscillation count, and error rate — 2026-03-20
Phase 3: Expand to 5% over 72h if no alerts; auto-rollback triggers on >5% 99th latency regression or >3x kernel-switch rate — 2026-03-23
Phase 4: Full rollout with staged regional expansion and post-rollout verification dashboard — 2026-03-31
